{{pagebanner|Colosseo di Roma banner.jpg|pgname=Colosseo, Rome}}
The '''Colosseo''' district is the heart of ancient [[Rome]] and the [[Roman Empire]]. It has the ''Colosseum'', the ''Forum'', and the ''Capitoline Museum''.

Via dei Fori Imperiali cuts through the centre of the Rome/Colosseo district, connecting Piazza Venezia with the Colosseum. It is well served by buses, although if you are into serious sightseeing you are likely to want to walk instead as the Roman Forum is on your right for most of the journey. After the Colosseum, the road becomes Via Labicana and takes you close to [[Rome/Esquilino-San Giovanni| San Giovanni]]. Buses serving Via dei Fori Imperiali include No. 75, which connects Termini Station with [[Rome/Aventino-Testaccio| Aventino- Testaccio]] and No. 85, which connects Piazza San Silvestro in the [[Rome/Modern Center|Modern Center]] (close to the Trevi Fountain) with San Giovanni. The {{marker|type=go|name={{station|Colosseum|B}}|lat=41.89146|long=12.49148}} metro station is two stops from Termini station in the direction of [[Rome/South|EUR]]. It will also be a stop for the new, and very much delayed, Line {{rint|rome|C}}, and the Colosseum end of the Via dei Fori Imperiali is made unattractive by the construction site.

==== Tickets====
When visiting the Colosseum in late spring, summer, or early fall, it is not unusual to see long lines at the entrance, where the admission fee is €18. The ticket is valid for 24 hours (updated September 2024) and includes admission to the Roman Forum, Palatine Hill, and the Colosseum.

It is possible to purchase an admission to the Palatine Hill (or the Roman Forum) for the same sum, which also provides direct access to the Colosseum via an automated entrance.
[[File:Panoramic photograph of interior of Colosseum.jpg|thumb|Colosseum interior]]
The ticket for the Colosseum, Roman Forum and the Palatine Hill (one ticket for all three sites) can be ordered online from the [http://www.coopculture.it/en/colosseo-e-shop.cfm official ticket office] and printed at home. The ticket is valid for 24 hours, starting from when you've first used it to enter either site. Even with the printed tickets you do have to stand in the line for the Colosseum, since there is a security check first. This line goes quite fast and isn't nearly as long as the line for the ticket office. When you have passed the security check, you can walk right to the ticket barriers. People who bought the ticket at the Colosseum have a small (metro style) ticket with a magnetic band. Your printed tickets won't fit in the machine. Therefore, make sure you use a barrier with a member of staff attending to it, they can scan your ticket with a hand scanner and let you pass. If no staff member is at the ticket barriers, go to the reservations office at the right, near the barrier.

If you already have a ticket (from the Colosseum or Roman Forum or printed at home) and want to visit the Palatine Hill, make sure you don't stand in line at the entrance at Via di San Gregorio. The entrance near the Arch of Titus is closed. The line at the entrance is for people without a ticket. If you have a ticket, enter the entrance building at the right side of the line. People with small tickets issued at the Colosseum can use the automated ticket barrier at the right side in the building, people who have home printed tickets should use the entrance on the left in the building, right after the ticket office. There is a member of staff with a hand scanner who can scan your ticket.

====Guided tours====
Near the Arch of Titus at the entrance to the Roman Forum, you might be approached by young, native-English speakers (often students) offering you free guided tours of the Forum. This is not a scam and is done as a way for tour companies to promote their other tours (i.e. at the end of the free tour, the guide hands out a brochure telling you about other tours around town that do cost). Even if you're not interested in the other tours, take the free one and you'll learn a lot about the most important archaeological site in the city. Another option is to prebook an official guided tour.

===Other landmarks===
* {{see
| name=Arch of Constantine | alt=Arco di Costantino | url= | email=
| address= | lat=41.88977 | long=12.49066 | directions=
| phone= | tollfree=
| hours= | price=Free to view
| wikipedia=Arch of Constantine | image=RomeConstantine'sArch03.jpg | wikidata=Q5786
| content=Located a short walk west of the Colosseum, this well-preserved monumental arch was erected (soon after 315) to commemorate the victory of Constantine, the first Christian emperor, over his rival Maxentius at the Battle of the Milvian Bridge in 312. In general design, the Arch of Constantine imitates the century-earlier Arch of Septimius Severus (nearby in the Forum). The three arches are decorated utilizing mainly materials plundered from other imperial monuments by Trajan, Hadrian and Marcus Aurelius. The quality of its sculptural decoration, however, betrays the slow degradation that Classical Roman sculpture had experienced in the 3rd century AD.
}}

In the centre of the square you can admire an exact copy of the Statue of Marcus Aurelius on horseback; the original is kept in one of the two museums, to preserve it from pollution.

These baths were built on the top of the ruins of '''Domus Aurea''' - the Golden House of Nero (the Colosseum was built on the drained site of Nero's lake). The area underneath the park contains an enormous area from Nero's villa. It was restored at great expense in the 1980s and 1990s, opened to the public, and then closed again after a few years when it began to leak!

| address=Via degli Astalli, 16 | lat=41.895833 | long=12.479722 | directions=Piazza del Gesù; not far from Piazza Venezia towards Largo di Torre Argentina
| phone=+39 06 69 70 01 | tollfree=
| hours=07:00-12:00, 16:00-19:00 | price=
| wikipedia=Church of the Gesù | image=Il Gesu.jpg | wikidata=Q719794
| content=This is one of the two main Jesuit churches in Rome, the other being the nearby Sant'Ignazio. The interior is Mannerist art on steroids. Simply astounding.
}}
* {{see | name=San Nicola in Carcere | alt= | url=http://www.vicariatusurbis.org/?page_id=188&ID=835 | email= | address= | lat=41.891111 | long=12.48 | directions= | phone= | tollfree= | fax= | hours= | price=€3 | wikipedia=San Nicola in Carcere | image=San Nicola in Carcere front.jpg | wikidata=Q2145580 | lastedit=2015-12-05 | content=Church built on the site of three Roman pagan temples, which can be explored underground for a small fee paid at a desk near the church entrance.
}} {{Dead link|date=October 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}
* {{see
| name=Basilica dei Santi Giovanni e Paolo al Celio | alt= | url=https://www.basilicassgiovanniepaolo.it/ | email=
| address=Clivo di Scauro 15 | lat=41.88648 | long=12.49202 | directions=
| phone=+39 06 700 57 45 | tollfree=
| hours= | price=
| wikipedia=Santi Giovanni e Paolo al Celio | wikidata=Q1586946
| lastedit=2021-10-10
| content=According to the legendary passio, two brothers, John and Paul, who were officials at the imperial court, suffered martyrdom in 362 in their home on the Caelian hill, during the reign of emperor Flavius Claudius Julianus. This basilica dedicated to these two Roman officers was erected starting from 398 and was used first as a domus ecclesiae by the Christian community.
}}
[[Image:SPrassede volta SZeno.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Mosaic at Santa Prassede]]
* {{see
| name=Santa Prassede | alt= | url=https://santaprassede.wordpress.com/ | email=basilicas.prassede@libero.it
| address=Via di S. Prassede, 9/A | lat=41.896111 | long=12.498611 | directions=leaving Santa Maria Maggiore walk very briefly down Via Merulana and take first right; S. Prassede is accessed by a side entrance straight ahead
| phone= | tollfree=
| hours=Open daily for visits: 10:00-12:00, 16:00-18:00; mass at 18:00 | price=Free
| wikipedia=Santa Prassede | image=Interior of Basilica di Santa Prassede, Rome.JPG | wikidata=Q733890
| content=Fantastic Byzantine mosaics and some other interesting artwork. Not to be missed. 30 minutes are sufficient for a relaxed visit.
}}
* {{see
| name=Santa Pudenziana | alt= | url=http://www.stpudenziana.org/ | email=
| address=Via Urbana 160 | lat=41.898611 | long=12.495556 | directions=2 blocks northwest of Santa Maria Maggiore
| phone=+39 338 1218541 | tollfree=
| hours=Opening hours for visiting: Mon-Sat: 09:00-11:30; otherwise, you can try to reserve a time to visit by calling | price=
| wikipedia=Santa Pudenziana | image=Santa Pudenziana - portale.jpg | wikidata=Q1526417
| content=A very ancient church named after a saint who was in 1969 removed from the Roman Catholic calendar of saints for the lack of details of her life. But the church retains the name and is well worth visiting for an excellent 4th-century mosaic and attractive decorations on the facade. Visiting hours are short, but if you arrive close to 11:30, try talking to the attendant if you see him, and he might let you visit for a few minutes. The church is small, so 15 minutes should be long enough to see and absorb everything.
}}

===Museums and galleries===
[[Image:Colossus.JPG|thumb|right|Colossus of Constantine, Capitoline Museum]]
* {{see
| name=Musei Capitolini | alt=Capitoline Museums | url=http://www.museicapitolini.org | email=info.museicapitolini@comune.roma.it
| address=Piazza del Campidoglio | lat=41.893056 | long=12.4825 | directions=
| phone=+39 06-6710-2071 | tollfree= | fax=
| hours=open Tue-Sun 09:00-19:00 | price=Ordinary €15.00
| wikipedia=Capitoline Museums | image=Muzeum Kapitolinskie.JPG | wikidata=Q333906
|lastedit=2021-01-04| content=The two museums are on opposite sides of the Piazza del Campidoglio, It is recommended to [http://www.ticketclic.it book tickets online]
}}
** {{see
| name=Museo Capitolino | alt=Capitoline Museum | url=http://www.museicapitolini.org/sede/piazza_e_palazzi/palazzo_nuovo | email=
| address= | lat=41.893594 | long=12.483164 | directions=
| phone= | tollfree= | fax=
| hours= | price=
| image=Roma-Palazzo Nuovo 1.jpg | wikidata=Q283153
| content=Built in the 17th century to a design based on an architectural sketch by Michelangelo. Highlights include the ancient Colossus of Constantine statue (the Colosseum was probably named for another giant statue, the Colossus of Nero which stood near the Flavian Amphitheatre as the Colosseum was originally known), ''The Dying Gaul'', a magnificent marble sculpture that copies a bronze Greek original of the 3rd century BC and the ''Capitoline Venus''. It also contains the remarkable original gilt bronze equestrian statue of emperor Marcus Aurelius (the one in the piazza is a replica).
}}
** {{see
| name=Palazzo dei Conservatori | alt=Palace of the Conservators | url= | email=
| address= | lat=41.892997 | long=12.482811 | directions=
| phone= | tollfree= | fax=
| hours= | price=
| image=Muzeum Kapitolinskie.JPG | wikidata=Q64103
| content=Also based on a Michelangelo architectural plan, this compact gallery is well endowed in classical sculpture and paintings. Highlights include the small 1st-century-BC bronze ''Lo Spinario'', a Greek statue of a little boy picking a thorn from his foot; the ''Lupa Capitolina'' (Capitoline Wolf), a rare Etruscan bronze statue probably dating from the 5th century BC; and (in the entrance courtyard), the massive head, hands, foot and kneecap from a colossal statue of Constantine the Great. The palace also contains a Pinacoteca (Picture Gallery) with paintings mainly from the 16th and 17th centuries - highlights include: Caravaggio's Fortune-Teller and his curious John the Baptist; The Holy Family, by Dosso Dossi; Romulus and Remus, by Rubens; and Titian's Baptism of Christ.
}}
* {{see | name=National Museum of the Palazzo di Venezia | alt=Museo Nazionale del Palazzo di Venezia | url=http://museopalazzovenezia.beniculturali.it/index.php?it/1/museo-nazionale-del-palazzo-di-venezia | email= | address=V. del Plebiscito, 118 | lat=41.896183 | long=12.481567 | directions= | phone=+39 06 6780131 | tollfree= | fax= | hours=Tue-Sun 08:30-19:30, ticket sales end 18:30 | price=€5, €2.50 for EU citizens aged 18-25 | wikipedia=Museo nazionale del Palazzo di Venezia | image=Roma-palazzovenezia02.jpg | wikidata=Q1954305 | content=In the very heart of the city center, the building was for centuries ago the seat of the Venice embassy. Today it houses a museum and art galleries.
}} {{Dead link|date=November 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}
* {{see | name=Palazzo Doria Pamphilj | alt=Doria Pamphilj Gallery | url=http://www.dopart.it/roma | email= | address=Piazza del Collegio Romano, 2; entrance: Via del Corso, 305 | lat=41.897669 | long=12.481145 | directions=bus 64, 81,85, 117, 119, 492 | phone=+39 06 6797323 | tollfree= | fax= | hours=09:00-19:00 (last admittion 18:00) | price=€12 | wikipedia=Doria Pamphilj Gallery | image=Roma-palazzodoriapamphili.jpg | wikidata=Q1203458 | lastedit=2016-12-19 | content=Good collection of Renaissance and Baroque art, including by Velasquez, Titian, Raphael, and Bernini, all owned by the Doria Pamphilj family. Excellent audio guides really bring the paintings to life.
}} {{Dead link|date=October 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}

==Buy==
* {{buy
| name=Archeo Art | alt= | url= | email=
| address=Via del Teatro di Marcello | lat=41.893364 | long=12.481321 | directions=Not far from the bottom of the Campidoglio steps
| phone= | tollfree= | fax=
| hours= | price=
| content=This shop sells beautiful reproductions of ancient sculptures; not the tacky kitsch sold by many of the street vendors, but museum quality miniatures that look incredibly close to the real things. Not cheap, but definitely unique and classy souvenirs. Also stocks reproductions of ancient Roman arms and armour, including full centurion outfits!
}}
